The petitioner is before this Court challenging the prosecution initiated against him in
C.C.No.1651/2015 for the offence punishable under Sections 323, 504, 506, 498A of Ipc pending
trial before the
Additional Civil Judge (Jr.Dn.) & JMFC Court, Maddur, Mandya district.
2. The respondent No.2 is the wife of the petitioner.
The respondent No.2 informed the respondent No.1 on 02.03.2015 that her marriage with the petitioner was solemnized five years ago before the Sub-registrar.
She claimed that her husband and in-laws were very avaricious and greedy.

She alleged that after the marriage, her husband and in-laws took away her gold ornaments and NC:
2023:KHC:28941 money.
She claimed that despite all the cruelty meted out, she lived with her husband and in-laws.
She alleged that her husband and her in-laws threw her out of the house and thereafter, she and her son started residing with her mother.
She claimed that her husband visited her at her mother's house and caused physical and mental cruelty and used to abuse and treat her badly.
She alleged that her husband had an illicit relationship with another woman.
She alleged that she was physically abused by her husband who pestered her for a divorce, so that he could marry another woman.
She alleged that her in-laws were all supporting her husband and also used to suspect her fidelity.
She alleged that her husband did not take care of her and her son and that her mother was looking after all the expenses.

She alleged that for the sake of money, her husband had attempted to kill her and her son in respect of which, she informed the emergency services on the helpline and that the police arrived at the scene and directed to go to a hospital.
She alleged that her husband insisted her to get money and gold ornaments from her mother and that only then he would live with her.
Based on this, the respondent No.1 registered Cr. No.75/2015 for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506, 109, 114, 143, read with 149 of IPC.

sentences.text: After an investigation the respondent No.1 filed a charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504, 323 and 506 of IPC.
The trial court took cognizance for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 of IPC and registered C.C.No.1651/2015 and issued process.
5. The petitioner being arraigned as accused No.1 has filed this petition challenging the prosecution launched against him and the order taking cognizance.
6. The learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the respondent No.2 had vaguely alleged some incidents but did not give specific details as to the date of commission of alleged crime.
He submitted that there was neither any demand for dowry nor was the respondent No.2 harassed by her.

He contended that the petitioner is a qualified doctor and the fact that he married the respondent no.2 before the NC: 2023:KHC:28941 Sub-Registrar, was proof of the fact that the petitioner did not expect any money or dowry from the respondent No.2.
He claimed that the respondent No.2 was earlier married to Giridar D.M. on 12.03.2008 and that marriage too was broken.
He alleged that the respondent No.2 had also lodged a similar complaint against Giridar D.M. and his family members, where a charge sheet was filed.
He therefore, contended that respondent No.2 is in the habit of lodging false complaints accusing her spouse of cruelty, demand of dowry etc.,
He therefore, contended that the impugned prosecution is a clear abuse of process of law and deserves to be set at naught.
7. The respondent No.2 though served with notice, has not appeared.
8. A perusal of the charge sheet discloses that CWs.2 to 5 were the eye witnesses to certain incidents that happened between petitioner and respondent No.2.
They have spoken of specific overt-acts committed by the petitioner, which constitutes an offence under Sections 498A, 323 and 506 of IPC.

The claim of the petitioner that he is NC: 2023:KHC:28941 implicated in the case is a defence available to him before the trial court and prosecution cannot be quashed on his claim that he is implicated in a false case.
As the charge sheet is already filed and there are material to justify the prosecution to continue, this Court cannot exercise jurisdiction to set at naught the prosecution.
It is however open for the petitioner to seek discharge in accordance with law.
Hence, petition lacks merit and is dismissed.
